blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Projects monitored by the country’s investment promotion agencies exceeded their investment commitments by 40 percent in 2024, with P246.9 billion poured in against a combined target of P176.5 billion, according to the Fiscal Incentives Review Board (FIRB). In its latest annual report for 2025, the FIRB said 86 percent, or 352, of the 407 projects monitored for investment capital commitments met or exceeded their obligations. READ: DOF eyes faster passage of multinational minimum tax bill Among these compliant projects, the FIRB approved 19, which collectively invested P125.2 billion against a target of P91 billion.
